stories.title: Eight rescued as fire breaks out in Mumbai Central building
stories.summary: Eight people, including an elderly woman and two toddlers, were rescued after a fire broke out in a residential building in Mumbai Central shortly after midnight on Sunday. A senior station officer of the Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) sustained a cut injury to his hand while battling the blaze.

stories.title: Bombay HC calls 300-plus Diwali fire incidents in Mumbai alarming, mulls wider ban
stories.summary: The Bombay High Court has expressed concern over more than 300 fire incidents reported in Mumbai during Diwali , along with rising noise and air pollution, and indicated that it may consider stricter restrictions on bursting firecrackers across the city. A division bench of Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale made the observations on Thursday while hearing petitions concerning noise and environmental pollution during festivals.

stories.title: BMC seeks nod to pay Rs 3.2cr metro cess to clear path for textile museum in Mazgaon
stories.summary: The payment is to be made to the Mumbai city collector’s office for the cess applicable on the land transfer document. 34-sqm mill to BMC on Jan 7, 2009, under Regulation 58 of Development Control Rules, 1991, for its development as a recreation ground. In Dec 2016, the state urban development department (UDD) directed that 44,000sqm of the land be reserved for a recreation ground and a textile museum.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at Navi Mumbai oil warehouse, spreads to two buildings
stories.summary: A major fire broke out at an oil warehouse in the Mefco Market area of Turbhe in Navi Mumbai, prompting an emergency response from local fire brigade teams. He said the fire control room received a call reporting that a shop had caught fire, following which a fire crew was immediately dispatched to the spot.

stories.title: Roadwork pit, bus crash claim 2 lives in Raigad
stories.summary: Two road accidents in Raigad within 24 hours claimed the lives of two two-wheeler riders, with one of the crashes exposing alleged safety lapses at a road construction site. A 52-year-old motorcyclist died after his bike plunged into an unmarked excavation in Alibaug on Thursday evening, a pillion rider was killed when a speeding tourist bus rammed an Activa scooter in Nagothane on Friday morning.

stories.title: Eight rescued, firefighter injured in fire at south Mumbai residential building
stories.summary: Eight people, including two children, were rescued after a fire broke out at a four-storey residential building in south Mumbai in the early hours of Sunday. A firefighter sustained injuries during the rescue operation, officials said. 07 am at Hira Manzil, located on Gildar Lane near Navjivan Society in Mumbai Central.

stories.title: Western Railway motormen, train managers participate in WNC Navy Half Marathon
stories.summary: Train managers and motormen from Western Railway participated in the WNC Navy Half Marathon 2026 in Mumbai on Sunday, November 22, completing the 5 km and 10 km running categories. The railway employees took part in the event despite their demanding operational schedules, which involve ensuring the safe movement of trains throughout the year.

stories.title: FDA seizes adulterated oil and rotten betel nuts, suspends restaurant licences
stories.summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) took action against 19 establishments following raids over the past week, suspending 17 licences and imposing penalties in two cases. Around 10 of these eateries and storage centres fall under the Mumbai Division. Action was also taken against five more establishments during other FDA drives.

stories.summary: 10pm. 58pm will run on the slow corridor till Thane before being re-diverted to the fast line at Mulund. 40 pm. 35pm on Sunday for maintenance of tracks, signalling and overhead equipment. Slow trains will run on fast lines during the block.

stories.summary: Vanrai police traced and rescued two minor brothers, aged 10 and eight, within hours of registering a missing persons case after they went missing from their home in Goregaon East. 30 pm and 10 pm on November 20 when their mother, Seema Shivdhani Gupta, 30, asked them to return home.

stories.title: BMC to pay ₹3.17 crore Metro cess to secure United Mills land for museum, recreation ground
stories.summary: 34 square metres of land belonging to the defunct India United Mills No. 2 and 3 in Mazagaon, also known as Indu Mills, to the civic body. The land is earmarked for a recreation ground and a textile museum. The proposal, which has received administrative approval, will be placed before the BMC standing committee on Wednesday.

stories.title: Security firm Topsgrup’s HQ goes under hammer at ₹15.6 crore
stories.summary: Once the nerve centre of security services firm Topsgrup, its former head office in Goregaon East is now headed for auction. 49 crore in dues through the sale of the property. 61 crore. 10-sq-ft) leasehold plot at Royal Palms, next to Piccadilly Apartment 1.

stories.title: Shah Rukh Khan calls for dialogue over violence at Global Peace Honours event, pays tribute to victims of 26/11 and Pahalgam attack
stories.summary: Actor Shah Rukh Khan delivered a powerful speech at the Global Peace Honours event held in Mumbai on Saturday. The actor called for choosing dialogue over violence and trust over fear to transform hatred into love, saying that peace was a "decision and a promise" that everyone must fulfil every day.

stories.title: Viral video shows minors assaulting man and woman at Kurla garden
stories.summary: A group of minors allegedly assaulted a young man and a woman at a public garden in the eastern suburb of Kurla in Mumbai. A video of the incident has also gone viral on social media, police said on Saturday. An official said that the attack took place at Pramod Mahajan Garden behind a mall in Kurla West, as per PTI.

stories.title: BMC scraps underground passage below Mahalaxmi Racecourse, ₹702-crore Metro-Coastal Road link to be redesigned
stories.summary: Amid opposition from architects and urban planners to Mahalaxmi Racecourse’s proposed redevelopment as part of the big-ticket Central Park project, BMC has decided to scrap all underground construction below the iconic landmark. The link, which was originally planned to pass beneath the racecourse, will now run entirely above ground adjoining the walking pathway of the racecourse stretch.

stories.title: Thief breaks into St Andrew’s Church, steals ₹15,000 in donation money
stories.summary: A thief broke into St Andrew’s Church in Bandra (west) and stole the cash from five donation boxes, leaving the local community shaken. According to the First Information Report (FIR) filed by parish priest Father Nigel Barrett, the theft took place between 11 pm on Friday and 5 am on Saturday after the burglar broke open a window and gained entry to the church.

stories.title: Mid-day lensmen shine as photographs make it to Mumbai's 2027 calendar
stories.summary: The photographs of mid-day lensmen Atul Kamble and Satej Shinde feature in Mumbai’s Essence to Grace the 2027 calendar of the Mumbai Marathi Patrakar Sangh ! Twelve outstanding images were picked from 401 entries filed by 42 participants (38 photojournalists, two video journalists, and two journalists).

stories.title: Mumbai traffic police book 40,210 motorists for wrong-side driving in 2026
stories.summary: Mumbai’s two-wheeler riders are increasingly driving on the wrong side of the road, with the traffic police booking 40,210 offenders in 2026 so far — more than three times the number recorded in the entire previous year. The spike has prompted a citywide crackdown, with all 41 traffic police divisions instructed to take strict action against violators.

stories.title: Mid-day photographers Atul Kamble and Satej Shinde feature in Mumbai Marathi Patrakar Sangh's 2027 calendar
stories.summary: The photographs of mid-day lensmen Atul Kamble and Satej Shinde feature in Mumbai’s Essence to Grace the 2027 calendar of the Mumbai Marathi Patrakar Sangh ! stories.title: Mumbai LIVE: Vanrai police rescue missing brothers aged 10 and 8 within hours
stories.summary: Vanrai police traced and safely rescued two minor brothers, aged 10 and eight, within a few hours of registering a missing persons case after they went missing from their home in Goregaon East. The children were found sleeping on iron beams at a railway construction site behind Ram Mandir railway station.

stories.title: BMC drops underground development at Mahalaxmi Racecourse
stories.summary: The civic administration has decided to scrap the ambitious underground component of the reimagined Mahalaxmi Racecourse plan, signalling a victory for urban planners and architects advocating for the city of Mumbai. While overground landscaped gardens and recreational spaces will remain part of the plan, Olympic-level sports facilities and a massive parking bay, which were to occupy two underground levels, have been dropped.

stories.title: ‘Women are the first to bear the brunt of a drought’
stories.summary: For nearly 30 years, the Mann Deshi Foundation (MDF) has supported livelihoods and worked at building economic resilience in households in the drought-prone Mann Taluka, spanning Satara, Sangli and Solapur districts. After running cattle camps in earlier droughts, constructing check dams and rejuvenating wells, it has now launched a nine-month water crisis mitigation and livelihood protection plan for one of the state’s worst droughts ever.

stories.title: 2 months after schoolmate sought PM Modi’s help, ‘land grab’ to be probed
stories.summary: On Wednesday, Varunkumar Sahare, Joint District Registrar of the Stamp and Registration Department (Thane Rural), ordered an investigation into the registration of land Asgarbhai Vohra, 81, has owned since 1989, but was allegedly encroached via fraud. The inquiry will be conducted by the Sub-Registrar (Bhiwandi). The dispute relates to a 2,810-sq m plot purchased by Vohra 37 years ago.

stories.title: Two dogs and ‘50 dog bites’: A housing society takes the BMC to court
stories.summary: For many residents of Shivalik Towers, a housing society in Kandivali East, life has changed over the last year. Children, the elderly, and members of the society staff have had to think twice before stepping out after the complex reported as many as 50 dog bites in a year from two stray dogs in the vicinity.

stories.title: Japan-style township planned around Virar bullet train station
stories.summary: A congested railway suburb could soon be reimagined on the lines of Japan’s Sapporo city. The Vasai-Virar City Municipal Corporation (VVCMC) is set to develop a 464-hectare township around the under-construction Virar bullet train station, making it the first civic body in Maharashtra to announce such a plan.

stories.title: Landlord’s criminal case cannot block med facility, rules HC
stories.summary: Patients cannot be denied access to a medical facility because the owner of its premises is facing a criminal case, the Bombay High Court has said, directing the state to clear a proposed PET-CT scan centre’s permissions within a week.

stories.title: Oil warehouse goes up in flames in Vashi; no injuries reported
stories.summary: Explosions from bursting oil drums, towering flames and thick black smoke lit up the Vashi-Turbhe industrial belt on Sunday night as a massive fire tore through an edible oil warehouse, spreading to an adjoining cold-storage facility and threatening the nearby Gokul milk-packing centre. There were no reports of casualties.

stories.title: MMRDA asks BMC for revised Powai rd plan to protect 122 trees
stories.summary: A proposed road that threatened to cut through a six-acre green space in Powai could now be realigned, potentially saving 122 trees at Pramod Mahajan Garden. 4-metre-wide Development Plan (DP) road. The development comes after more than 3,000 residents and 35 housing societies campaigned against the proposed Development Plan (DP) road, which cuts through the six-acre garden in Hiranandani Gardens.

stories.title: Mumbai BJP wants BMC to maintain all open spaces, develop international sports facilities in 2-3 playgrounds in every ward
stories.summary: BJP functionaries met to discuss the management of open spaces in Mumbai. They agreed to maintain all open spaces entirely under BMC control. The decision reflects the party's commitment to its election manifesto. Plans were made to develop international sports facilities using BMC funds and CSR contributions. Additionally, the scope of BKLP will expand to manage these new facilities.

stories.title: Bhopal Arera Colony Sealing Row Reaches Supreme Court As Residents Allege Shops Reopened Despite BMC Action
stories.summary: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): The Supreme Court will hear the Bhopal sealing case on Monday, with residents questioning the action taken report (ATR) submitted by the Bhopal Municipal Corporation (BMC). Petitioners and residents of Arera Colony have alleged that misleading affidavits were submitted before the court regarding the sealing of commercial establishments in residential areas.

stories.title: Wait, walk, or pay more: How Mumbai’s shrunken BEST fleet is draining commuters
stories.summary: In Mumbai, the ongoing decline in bus services is leading to increased travel times and frustration among commuters. With cuts to routes and a smaller bus fleet, residents—especially students and daily-wage earners—are turning to more expensive transportation methods, straining their budgets. As inflation rises, accessibility issues deepen. Authorities have plans for a fleet expansion, yet many commuters feel left in the lurch amid growing difficulties.

stories.title: Bhopal Water Contamination Scare As 6 Borewells Test Positive For Coliform Bacteria In Ashoka Colony, BMC Shuts All 12
stories.summary: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Bhopal Municipal Corporation (BMC) has intensified water sampling across the locality from Sunday, after the detection of contaminated groundwater in Ashoka Colony, adjoining Noor Mahal and Nawab Siddiq Hasan Khan Talab in the old city. The civic body had detected total coliform bacteria in water samples from Ashoka Colony on Saturday.

stories.title: FSSAI orders prosecution against Bisleri International for unsafe packaged drinking water
stories.summary: Food regulator FSSAI on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International, as it found its sample of packaged drinking water "unsafe". In a social media post, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) said it has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd regarding "unsafe packaged drinking water".

stories.title: Bisleri under FSSAI scanner: 2 water samples found unsafe, prosecution sanctioned
stories.summary: FSSAI has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri over a sample of packaged drinking water that was found non-compliant with prescribed bromate limits and declared unsafe under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Referral Food Laboratory too declared it unsafe after detecting polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. Vasant Masala Pvt Ltd was prosecuted after its chilli powder was found to contain difenoconazole, a pesticide residue, above the allowed limit.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu moves SC seeking review of Nov 20 ‘Karthigai Deepam’ order
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has moved the Supreme Court seeking a review of its November 20 order allowing the “Karthigai Deepam” to be lit as a one-time measure at the disputed stone pillar, or the deepathoon, atop the Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai .

stories.title: Bengal BJP MLA Rekha Patra critical after suspected pesticide poisoning
stories.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Hingalganj in West Bengal’s North 24 Parganas, Rekha Patra, was on Sunday (November 22, 2026) admitted to a private hospital in the city after falling ill from suspected pesticide poisoning. The MLA was admitted to Basirhat Subdivision Hospital, from where she was shifted to the private facility.

stories.title: Police in Karnataka prevent Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee chief Y.S. Sharmila from entering disputed property
stories.summary: S. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, from entering a disputed property in Yelahanka, citing an interim injunction order issued by a court in Devanahalli. Ms. Sharmila was stopped by the police at Bagalur Road in Yelahanka while she was travelling towards Yelahanka Palace at Kattigenahalli village in Jala hobli, Bengaluru North taluk.

stories.title: Raut alleges Rs 150 cr per MP to pass Delimitation Bill; BJP responds
stories.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Sunday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of attempting to buy MPs from other political parties to secure the numbers required to pass the proposed Delimitation Bill in Parliament. He alleged that the BJP was offering Rs 150 crore for each MP who switches sides, reported the IANS.

stories.title: Maharashtra government withdraws Bombay High Court petition against FSSAI
stories.summary: The Maharashtra government has withdrawn its petition filed before the Bombay High Court challenging the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) over what it had described as an encroachment on the state’s food safety enforcement powers. The petition, filed in October by FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, came up for hearing on November 21.

stories.title: Tiger Shroff attack: AICWA chief says daily wage workers bear brunt of security concerns
stories.summary: A cloud of fear has loomed over the Hindi film industry in the past month, after actor Tiger Shroff was attacked in a firing incident on October 18. Since then, actors Amitabh and Abhishek Bachchan, and Saif Ali Khan have received threats . According to the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA), in light of the recent incidents, many film shoots are being postponed or shifted to prioritise the safety of actors.

stories.title: Accidents leave 4 dead in Mohali, Panchkula | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: As many as four lives were snuffed out in separate road accidents, three of them hit-and-runs, in Mohali and Panchkula districts. The first accident occurred near Tabar village on the Panchkula-Yamunanagar national highway on Sunday afternoon, claiming the life of a 63-year-old Shimla native.

stories.title: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies of cardiac arrest in Delhi
stories.summary: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute, who was elected to the Upper House earlier this year, died following a cardiac arrest at a hospital in New Delhi, family sources said on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Mr. Wadkute was admitted to AIIMS in the national capital on November 20 after complaining of a cough.

stories.title: Amritsar grenade attack: US-based Happy Passia, 8 others declared proclaimed offenders
stories.summary: US-based gangster-terrorist associated with Babbar Khalsa International (BKI), Harpeet Singh alias Passia, and eight others have been declared proclaimed offenders (POs) in connection with a grenade attack at a police station in Punjab’s Gurdaspur in April last year. The order for declaring them POs was passed by a special National Investigation Agency (NIA) court in Mohali on Saturday based on a request by the agency.

stories.title: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya calls for protest over attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh
stories.summary: West Bengal Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) president Samik Bhattacharya on Sunday (November 22, 2026) called for a protest against the alleged persecution of Hindus in Bangladesh . “Blood is being shed in Bangladesh, and it is our brothers who are suffering. As a Bengali Hindu, I believe we must take to the streets,” the BJP leader told media persons.

stories.title: Maharashtra scales down tree plantation drive amid severe drought, says Fadnavis
stories.summary: Maharashtra has scaled down its tree-plantation drive this year due to acute water shortages caused by severe drought conditions across several districts, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis said on Saturday. Speaking at an event in the presence of spiritual leader Sadhguru Jaggi Vasudev, Fadnavis said that 80-90 per cent of rural Maharashtra was facing drought and a severe water crisis.

stories.title: BJP accuses Tamil Nadu govt of ‘anti-hindu’ mindset over SC review plea on Karthigai Deepam
stories.summary: The BJP on Sunday said the Tamil Nadu government's move to seek a review of a Supreme Court order permitting the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp on November 24 as a one-time measure at Deepathoon reflects an "anti-Hindu and anti-Sanatan Dharma" mindset of the Congress and its allies.

stories.title: Centre prioritising border villages, 40 seeing reverse migration: Amit Shah in Arunachal Pradesh
stories.summary: Describing the development of border villages as a priority of the government, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday (November 22, 2026) said the upliftment of about 40 villages along the International Border in Arunachal Pradesh , under the Centre’s flagship Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP), ensured that many of those who moved out from these areas were returning.

stories.title: Manipur hooch tragedy toll rises to 17; sample sent to Kolkata lab
stories.summary: The death toll in Manipur’s hooch tragedy rose to 17 on Sunday (November 22, 2026), as the State government sent samples of the suspected spurious liquor produced locally to the National Food Laboratory in Kolkata for testing. Government spokesperson and MLA Thokchom Radheshyam Singh said 16 people who died after consuming the liquor were from Chandel district and one was from Kakching district.

Rickshaw Panchayat and its allied organizations have decided to stage protests at offices of legislators. “Bike taxis were encroaching upon the already dwindling earnings of auto drivers. Although there is currently no legal authorization for transporting passengers via two-wheelers (bike taxis), the administration lacks the political will to curb this practice.

stories.title: 24 civilians killed in fresh South Sudan violence | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: A weekend attack by opposition forces in volatile South Sudan killed 24 civilians, including seven children, local authorities said Sunday. The world's youngest country, which gained independence in 2011, has been torn apart by violence between rival political factions, often linked to ethnicity or cattle rustling.

stories.summary: Rekha Patra, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) legislator from West Bengal’s Hingalganj, was hospitalised on Saturday night with symptoms of food poisoning , health minister Sharadwat Mukherjee said on Sunday after visiting the private hospital in Kolkata where Patra was on a ventilator. “I inquired about her health.

stories.title: Woman arrested for retaliating against abusive husband, killing him
stories.summary: Unable to endure repeated beatings by her husband, a 31-year-old woman fought back during a violent quarrel at their Virugambakkam home, raining blows until he collapsed and died. Police said Hemavathi, 31, and her husband K Osuran alias Suresh, 35, a welder, who had married for love, lived in Gandhi Nagar with their five-year-old son.

stories.title: DTCP imposes penalty on 25 plot owners for violating construction ban | Hindustan Times
stories.summary: The enforcement wing of department of town and country planning (DTCP) on Sunday said that it has taken action against 25 plot owners in the Sushant Lok 1 and Sun City colonies for carrying out construction work, despite the restrictions imposed by the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) to curb air pollution in the Delhi-NCR region, officials said, adding that an environmental fine of ₹ 50,000 each was issued.

stories.title: Maharashtra to upgrade 3,832 anganwadis with smart classrooms, modern kitchens
stories.summary: Maharashtra will upgrade 3,832 anganwadi centres across the state under a government initiative to improve infrastructure and provide children with better learning facilities, Women and Child Development Minister Aditi Tatkare said on Sunday. The centres will be equipped with e-learning tools, rainwater harvesting systems, modern kitchens and other facilities as part of the plan to develop them into smart anganwadis.

stories.title: MPPSC Exams See Sharp Turnout Gap As 63% Skip Scientific Officer Test, 73% Appear For Agriculture Exam
stories.summary: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): The Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission (MPPSC) conducted two recruitment examinations on Sunday for vacant posts in different government departments, with a significant difference in the attendance of candidates. While only 37% of registered candidates appeared for the Scientific Officer examination, the Assistant Director (Agriculture) examination recorded an attendance of 73%.

stories.title: Indore Water Supply Gets ₹6.31 Crore Boost As New 35-Lakh-Litre Tank, 22-Km Pipeline Network To Benefit 4,496 Families
stories.summary: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): Western Indore is set to get a major boost to its water supply infrastructure with the construction of a new 35-lakh-litre-capacity water tank at Hawa Bangla and a 22-km distribution pipeline network. 31-crore project will benefit 4,496 domestic tap connections across three municipal wards. Mayor Pushyamitra Bhargav performed the 'bhoomipujan' of the Hawa Bangla water tank and distribution network project.

stories.title: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992 after flipping North Carolina seat
stories.summary: The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina. The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.

stories.title: US Intelligence Chief Says Putin Is 'Not America's Friend In Ukraine'
stories.summary: ""He is not America's friend in Ukraine. Trump later defended his remarks, arguing that "it's nice to have people that have 4,000 nuclear weapons as a friend as opposed to an enemy." stories.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
stories.summary: A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship on Sunday (November 22, 2026) at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war. The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.

stories.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
stories.summary: A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime. The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels.

stories.title: 3 killed and 1 wounded in shooting at Ohio baby shower; 1 man in custody, police say
stories.summary: Three people were killed and one was injured at an Ohio baby shower during an apparent domestic dispute, authorities said. Officers responded to a shooting Saturday evening at Pandora's Magical Events Venue in Parma, about 10 miles (16 kilometres) south of Cleveland, a police news release said. Authorities said one of the shooters, a 29-year-old man, was taken into custody, but he wasn't immediately charged.

stories.title: Italian jeweller and businessman Paolo Bulgari dies aged 89
stories.summary: Italian jeweller Paolo Bulgari, who helped turn his family's business into a global luxury brand, has died in Rome aged age 89. His family announced the news, remembering him as "the greatest jeweller of our time", according to Italian media. Paolo Bulgari was Chairman of the Bvlgari Group since 1984 and its jewellery pieces have adorned Hollywood stars and royalty including Diana, Princess of Wales.

stories.title: Yemen Houthis Claim Strikes On Saudi Arabias Rabigh Oil Refinery And Radar Facility Near Riyadh Amid
stories.summary: / @ferozwala Sanaa: Yemen's Houthi group said that it had carried out two military operations targeting an oil refinery on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast and a radar facility south of the capital Riyadh, amid escalating cross-border hostilities.

stories.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
stories.summary: An explosion has occurred on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port after a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said. The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government.

stories.title: China State Funds Ramp Up ETF Buying to Record as Rout Deepens
stories.summary: China’s state-backed funds poured a record amount of money into the market on Friday in another forceful attempt to stem a deepening selloff. Inflows into the nine exchange-traded funds known to be actively traded by the so-called national team totaled 90 billion yuan on Friday, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.

stories.title: Cargo ship bound for Russia's Kaliningrad hit by drones, Finland tightens security
stories.summary: google Add Al Jazeera on Rescue efforts are under way in the Gulf of Finland after a Russian cargo ship was hit by drones close to Russia’s maritime border. The ship, the Sparta II, is on fire and has now drifted into Finnish territorial waters, authorities say.

stories.title: Father, daughter detained by ICE at Seattle airport were travelling to family baptism, says lawyer
stories.summary: A father and daughter detained by masked immigration officers on an airport jet bridge in Seattle, causing chaos in front of other passengers, were heading to a family baptism ceremony in California, their lawyer said Sunday (November 22, 2026).

stories.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
stories.summary: The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides. Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22).

stories.title: Three killed and dozens missing after fire at Indonesian factory
stories.summary: At least three people have been killed and 36 are still missing after a fire at a confectionary factory in western Java on Saturday. Firefighters were still tackling some flames on Sunday, while rescuers searched for the missing in parts of the damaged building where workers were believed to be trapped.

stories.title: San Francisco is enjoying an AI boom, but worries about a crash are growing
stories.summary: Fuelling the growth is her new office dog-walking service Paw Perk, popular with some local AI start-ups. Her business is an example of how the AI boom in San Francisco is benefiting other sectors. The city saw an exodus of residents during the pandemic and its downtown was weakened by remote work, but it s now enjoying a rejuvenation, with AI being the major driver.

stories.title: US put 1,389 Indian children in custody in 4 years; none repatriated
stories.summary: The anti-immigration crackdown in US has swept 1,389 unaccompanied Indian children into custody since America’s FY23. The decline mirrors the trend for unaccompanied children of all nationalities. 1 lakh unaccompanied children in FY24, 29,584 in FY25, and 9,190 in FY26. People familiar with immigration networks in US said the decline could partly be linked to stricter enforcement and faster deportations.

stories.title: Australian music legend Molly Meldrum dies aged 83
stories.summary: The music promoter and broadcaster, born Ian Alexander Meldrum, helped define the nation's music tastes for decades, championing local artists like INXS and Kylie Minogue and global acts like Abba. Known for his chaotic demeanour and trademark Stetson hat, he interviewed an array of stars from King Charles to Elton John, who described Meldrum as the "single most important influence in Australian pop music".

stories.title: Miley Cyrus marries Maxx Morando in California ceremony
stories.summary: Miley Cyrus has married her partner of four years Maxx Morando during a ceremony in Palm Springs, California.
